scene.testo: In ancient Rome, your day started before the sun did. No coffee, no alarm clock, no snooze button. You got up in the dark, in the cold, and got dressed by feel. Within twenty minutes, you had to be standing outside a rich man's house.
Why? Because if you weren't there, you didn't eat that day. That's not an exaggeration. That was the system. For hundreds of years, this was daily life for hundreds of thousands of ordinary people.
We picture togas, marble and emperors giving speeches. The reality was louder, dirtier and stranger than any movie has ever shown you. And here's the part that breaks most people's brains.
The Romans did not have hours the way you do. So how did they know when to start, when to eat, when to stop? Would you survive a single day in their world?

descrizione:
What did people in ancient Rome actually do all day? Forget the movies. Daily life in ancient Rome began before sunrise, with ordinary Romans lining up outside a rich patron's house just to earn their daily bread.

In this animated history documentary, we explore the roman daily life of the poor and the powerful, from the crowded streets and the Roman Forum to the markets, the baths and the Colosseum. Discover how the patron system really worked and why missing the morning visit could mean going hungry.

If you love ancient history, Roman history and weird history facts, this video shows what life in ancient Rome was truly like.
